verses.1: The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, your family, and your father's house and go to the land I will show you.
verses.2: I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be a blessing to others.
verses.3: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse anyone who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you."
verses.4: So Abram left, just as the LORD had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran.
verses.5: Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, everything they owned, and all the people who had joined them in Haran. They set out for the land of Canaan, and they arrived there.
verses.6: Abram traveled through the land as far as Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were living in the land.
verses.7: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your offspring." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.8: From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and set up his tent between Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built another altar to the LORD and called on His name.
verses.9: Then Abram continued traveling south toward the Negeb.
verses.10: There was a severe famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a time.
verses.11: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "I know that you are a beautiful woman.
verses.12: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me but let you live.
verses.13: Please say that you are my sister so that things will go well for me because of you and my life will be spared."
verses.14: When Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
verses.15: When Pharaoh's officials saw her, they told Pharaoh how beautiful she was, and she was taken into Pharaoh's palace.
verses.16: Because of her, Pharaoh treated Abram well and gave him sheep, cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
verses.17: But the LORD sent serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
verses.18: Pharaoh called for Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me she was your wife?
verses.19: Why did you say she was your sister? I took her as my wife. Now here is your wife — take her and go."
verses.20: Pharaoh gave orders to his men, and they sent Abram away with his wife and everything he owned.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
